subject: Medicine
title: Acute Severe Asthma and COPD Exacerbations: Bedside Priorities
preview: Recognize respiratory failure early; assess work of breathing and mental status rather than relying only on wheeze.

sections.title: Find danger signs
points: Exhaustion, altered consciousness, inability to speak, reduced air movement or worsening hypoxemia require escalation.
Assess peak flow when appropriate without delaying treatment of an unstable patient.

sections.title: Manage by physiology
points: Use acute-asthma or COPD pathways matched to severity, gases, oxygenation and response.
Monitor for rising carbon dioxide or fatigue; noninvasive or invasive ventilation decisions are individualized.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A quiet chest can be ominous, not reassuring.
Routine unmonitored high-flow oxygen is not appropriate for every COPD exacerbation.

quickRevision: Severe asthma can present with minimal audible wheeze when airflow is critically restricted.
Initial treatment pathways include oxygen titration, rapid-acting inhaled bronchodilator therapy and systemic anti-inflammatory treatment when indicated.
COPD exacerbations require attention to hypercapnic risk, infection or cardiac triggers and possible ventilatory support.

quiz.question: Which sign may indicate life-threatening asthma despite reduced wheeze?
options: Normal speech and minimal work of breathing
quiz.explanation: A quiet chest with exhaustion. A quiet chest can be ominous, not reassuring.
